author: Wired

title: Mary Anne Franks Links Sexual Assault to Free Speech in Online Abuse Fight
content: Mary Anne Franks has spent years fighting against online abuse. When people are abused with impunity, she says, the message becomes “We do not care about women’s voices.”
summary: Mary Anne Franks has spent years fighting against online abuse. She says that when abuse goes unpunished, the message is “We do not care about women’s voices.”
author: Wired

title: Sony ULT Tower 7 party speaker $100 off at lowest price
content: Sony is offering a $100 discount on its ULT Tower 7 party speaker, which the source lists as one of its top party‑speaker picks and now at its lowest‑ever price. Buyers are encouraged to purchase the Tower 7 or its sibling models before their next fete.
summary: The Sony ULT Tower 7 is listed as a top party speaker. It is being offered at its lowest-ever price with a $100 discount, and sibling models are also available.
author: Wired

title: Baseus releases U2 Pro Outdoor camera with spotlight that tracks moving targets
content:
Baseus has announced the Security PrimeSentinel U2 Pro Outdoor 3K Dual Camera, a new AI‑assisted security camera that adds a motorized spotlight to its features. The spotlight’s focused beam follows moving targets, shining directly on them even as they run across a property, thereby indicating detection.

According to the announcement, the bright spotlight not only deters unwanted visitors but also enhances night‑time video quality, improving the likelihood that a subject can be identified. The company notes that the lighting can also be useful for household tasks after dark, such as taking a dog outside. The product joins Baseus’s existing lineup of AI‑driven security cameras.
summary: Baseus announced the Security PrimeSentinel U2 Pro Outdoor 3K Dual Camera, which features a motorized spotlight that follows moving targets across a property. The spotlight improves night‑time video quality and can assist with after‑hours tasks such as walking a dog.
author: The Verge

title: Google Home speakers downloading hundreds of gigabytes; fix rolling out
content:
Google Home speaker owners have reported that their devices are downloading large amounts of data in the background.  Reports from 9to5Google and several Reddit users over the past week describe the problem as continuous downloads that can reach hundreds of gigabytes, with one Redditor noting consumption of more than 200 GB per day.  The issue appears to be linked to a failure in correctly downloading and installing a firmware update on the speakers.

Google confirmed awareness of the bug. In a statement to 9to5Google the company said a fix is already rolling out and should address the problem for affected users.  The majority of the reports are associated with the newer Google Home models.
summary: Some Google Home speaker owners are experiencing a bug that causes the devices to continuously download hundreds of gigabytes of data, with one user reporting over 200 GB per day. Google said a fix is already rolling out to address the issue.
author: The Verge

title: Sceye airship completes US-Japan round-trip to test stratospheric cell tower
content:
A US‑based aerospace firm, Sceye, completed a round‑trip flight from New Mexico to Japan and back, marking the first stratospheric airship to cross the Pacific Ocean since the Graf Zeppelin’s 1929 nonstop journey. The flight, conducted over a month between August and September 2026, was intended to demonstrate the platform’s ability to serve as an airborne cell‑phone tower.

The uncrewed vehicle is buoyed by helium and propelled by an electric‑driven propeller, enabling it to resist strong winds and hover for extended periods. Top‑mounted solar panels and onboard batteries provide continuous power for stratospheric operations, allowing the airship to remain at roughly 60,000 feet—twice the altitude of typical air traffic and above the jet stream—while staying over a single area.

Sceye’s founder and CEO, Mikkel Frandsen, explained that the platform can operate day and night, recharging its batteries with sunlight and maintaining the same altitude and location. The successful trans‑Pacific test highlights the potential for lighter‑than‑air platforms to deliver communications services from the stratosphere.
summary: Sceye airship completes US-Japan round-trip to test stratospheric cell tower.
author: Ars Technica

title: DIY VR headsets can be built for a couple hundred dollars but stay niche
content:
Virtual reality’s market momentum has slowed after a resurgence that began with the 2016 Oculus Rift launch. Although early optimism suggested a large future for VR, AR, XR and the metaverse, development of new headsets has decelerated, and several companies—including Apple—have reduced or paused their projects.

Despite the overall slowdown, a handful of new consumer devices such as the Steam Frame and the Pimax Dream Air continue to appear. At the same time, interest has shifted toward the enthusiast community, where DIY VR builds are emerging as a niche activity. With a few hundred dollars in components, along with time spent soldering, flashing firmware and 3D‑printing parts, individuals can assemble their own headsets.

The author of the piece reports personal experience with this do‑it‑yourself approach, describing it as a “rollercoaster” that highlights both the excitement and the challenges of the process, and concluding that DIY VR remains a specialized pursuit.
summary: Development of new headsets has slowed, though releases such as the Steam Frame and Pimax Dream Air continue to appear. DIY VR headsets can be assembled for a couple hundred dollars using soldering, firmware flashing and 3D printing, but the required time and effort keep the practice a niche movement.
author: Ars Technica

title: HBO's Lanterns offers gritty superhero twist with 2016 Nebraska shooting plot
content: The trailers for HBO's DC Universe series Lanterns teased a show that eschewed the usual superhero hijinks in favor of a gritty realism more in the vein of True Detective or Slow Horses. Personally, I liked the change. My verdict: Ignore the review bombing ; it's wonderful. The season wrapped with an emotionally charged, almost elegiac finale that fully delivered on that initial promise. I've found the rebooted DC Universe films released thus far to be enjoyable but rather forgettable, even when the positives outweigh the negatives. But Lanterns is a shining beacon of what is possible when someone is allowed to get really creative within the genre. (Spoilers below, but no major reveals.) There are two primary storylines. The first takes place in 2016 with a mass shooting at a local football game in Rushville, Nebraska. Current Green Lantern Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) and his new trainee, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), get involved in the investigation, to the annoyance of Sheriff Kerry Kane (Kelly Macdonald), who initially doesn't think the case has any extraterrestrial connection. She is soon proved wrong when the suspect (an alien) self-detonates. Hal's power ring controls the damage, but the mystery remains. Read full article Comments
summary: The trailers for HBO's DC Universe series Lanterns teased a show that eschewed the usual superhero hijinks in favor of a gritty realism more in the vein of True Detective or Slow Horses. Personally, I liked the change.
author: Ars Technica

title: Chinese Zhuque-2E rocket debris lands in Minnesota farmer's cornfield
content:
A Chinese medium‑lift rocket launched from the Dongfeng commercial launch zone, which shares facilities with the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China, on September 15. The vehicle, identified as a Zhuque‑2E built by LandSpace, lifted off less than two hours before it began a deorbit maneuver that sent debris toward the United States.

The rocket’s flight lasted roughly 75 to 80 minutes and did not complete a full Earth orbit. After releasing ten satellites, the booster reignited its engine and entered a trajectory that produced streaks of fiery debris falling from the sky. Observers reported the debris moving north over Kansas, visible on the western horizon from Wisconsin, and eventually reaching the American Midwest.

Experts matched the timing, location and direction of the falling fragments to the September 15 Zhuque‑2E launch, confirming that the debris originated from the Chinese launch vehicle. The incident was widely shared on social media as the debris illuminated the night sky over the region.
summary: A Zhuque‑2E rocket built by LandSpace launched from Dongfeng in the Gobi Desert on September 15, released ten satellites, reignited its engine and deorbited after a 75‑80 minute flight without completing an orbit. Debris fell over Kansas, Wisconsin and Minnesota, landing in a farmer’s cornfield in Minnesota.
author: Ars Technica

title: Disney structures deal to acquire Character.AI staff and technology while sidestepping its lawsuits
content:
Character.AI filed for bankruptcy this week, a move that the company’s newly appointed chief executive described as aimed at reaching a “consensual resolution” with personal‑injury claimants and a group of states while maximizing asset value for shareholders. The filing also noted that the bankruptcy was intended to preserve the company’s remaining assets.

According to court documents, Disney has arranged to hire most of Character.AI’s staff, including its former chief executive Karandeep Anand, and may acquire the startup’s technology. The structure of the deal appears to leave the bankrupt entity responsible for the ongoing lawsuits and regulatory investigations that have surrounded Character.AI, allowing Disney to obtain the talent and technology without assuming those legal liabilities.
summary: Character.AI declared bankruptcy as part of a plan to resolve personal injury claims and regulatory investigations while preserving asset value. Disney’s arrangement will hire most of the staff, including former CEO Karandeep Anand, and obtain the technology, leaving the remaining company to handle existing legal liabilities.
author: Ars Technica

title: Florida DMV breach after police department stored login info insecurely
content:
The Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV) has begun notifying individuals whose driver’s license and motor‑vehicle records were accessed in a data breach. In a notice posted Friday, the agency said a “malicious actor” accessed certain department records on September 4, 2026 using compromised credentials. Law enforcement determined that the potentially affected information includes driver‑license data, motor‑vehicle data, document images and other personal details, though the department said there is “no evidence” the data has been misused.

FLHSMV is mailing letters to those identified as victims and is offering one year of credit‑monitoring services from Sontiq, Inc. The agency acknowledged that it may lack current contact information for many former Florida residents whose data remains stored, and those individuals can verify whether their information was compromised by emailing customerinquiry@flhsmv.
summary: Florida DMV breach after police department stored login info insecurely.
author: Ars Technica

title: Japan launches $578 million MMX mission to sample Martian moon Phobos
content:
Japan’s Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission lifted off on Monday, marking the start of a five‑year effort to land on Phobos, the larger of Mars’s two moons, and return material to Earth. The $578 million project aims to collect samples that could shed light on the Solar System’s formation.

The spacecraft was launched at 3:41 p.m. EDT (4:41 a.m. Japan Standard Time) from the Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan. It rode atop a 207‑foot‑tall (63‑meter) H3 launch vehicle, Japan’s flagship rocket, which featured a new configuration that includes four strap‑on solid rocket boosters, full‑throttle main engines and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the mission’s requirements. The MMX mission is described as Japan’s heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary undertaking to date.
summary: Japan launched the $578 million Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission on a H3 rocket from Tanegashima Space Center. The five‑year mission will land on Mars’s largest moon Phobos, collect samples and return them to Earth.
author: Ars Technica

title: Slate opens first showroom in Chicago as $24,950 electric pickup nears production
content:
Slate has opened its first retail location, the Slate Customer Experience Center, in Chicago’s Fulton Market District just northwest of the Loop. The showroom occupies a former Tesla store and is staffed by several former Tesla employees. According to the visit, the center allows prospective buyers to explore a prototype Slate Truck, view customization options, purchase Slate merchandise and place a pre‑order on the vehicle with a $300 deposit.

The Slate Truck is marketed as a bare‑bones electric pickup with a listed price of $24,950. It features plastic body panels, a minimalist interior, functional window winders and a projected driving range of 205 miles. The author experienced the truck firsthand, noting the ability to manually roll down the windows while seated in the cab.
summary: Slate opened its first showroom, the Slate Experience Center, in a former Tesla store in Chicago’s Fulton Market District near the Loop. The center lets visitors view a prototype and pre‑order the $24,950 Slate Truck, which has a projected 205‑mile range and features plastic panels, a minimalist interior and functional window winders.
author: Ars Technica

title: Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe says autonomy will enable radically different vehicle designs
content: Founder and CEO RJ Scaringe said that autonomous technology will let Rivian create vehicle designs that are radically different from the company’s current lineup of outdoors‑oriented SUVs and trucks. He believes autonomy will enable dramatically new forms for future models.
summary: Founder and CEO RJ Scaringe said autonomy will allow Rivian to build radically different kinds of vehicles. He noted this would differ from the outdoorsy SUVs and trucks the company currently makes.
author: TechCrunch

title: Mayor Zohran Mamdani says federal inaction on AI, urges New Yorkers to push back
content: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Monday night that the federal government has abdicated responsibility for artificial‑intelligence oversight. He urged New Yorkers to reject the notion that an AI takeover is inevitable and to demand regulations that protect the public and return control over the technology to citizens.
summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Monday night that the federal government has abdicated on AI. He urged New Yorkers to resist the narrative of an inevitable AI takeover and demand regulations that protect the public.
author: TechCrunch

title: Blackwall raises $100M, valuation hits $2.2B to fund security tools
content: Blackwall announced a $100 million financing round that values the company at $2.2 billion, a four‑fold increase from its prior valuation. The funding will support the development of security and filtering tools designed to help websites manage rising bot and AI traffic.
summary: Blackwall has raised $100 million at a $2.2 billion valuation. The money will support building security and filtering tools that help websites grapple with growing bot and AI traffic.
author: TechCrunch

title: Otter.ai raises $320 million from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund
content: Otter.ai, a meeting note‑taking tool, announced on Tuesday that it secured $320 million from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund, a growth fund that supplies capital to startups without equity dilution and ties returns to marketing spend outcomes. The company said the financing will support enterprise growth, go‑to‑market strategy, international expansion and product innovation.
summary: Otter.ai announced on Tuesday it has raised $320 million from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF). The company said the capital will be used for enterprise growth, go‑to‑market strategy, international expansion and product innovation.
author: TechCrunch

title: Yelp adds AI feature to call restaurants and check wait times for users
content: Yelp is adding a suite of new AI capabilities to its app. Among the features, the system can place a call to a restaurant to inquire about current wait times and can generate personalized recommendations that retain users’ stated preferences.
summary: Yelp is embedding numerous new AI features into its app. The features can call restaurants to check wait times and create personalized recommendations that remember user preferences.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI-generated Val Kilmer doppelganger appears in new western As Deep as the Grave
content:
A new western titled “As Deep as the Grave” features an AI‑generated likeness of a young Val Kilmer. In the trailer, the digital double delivers the line “Don’t fear the dead – and don’t fear me.” Director Coerte Voorhees says the version was created with the approval of Kilmer’s family, and the actor’s estate signed off on its use, noting his enthusiasm for technology that expands storytelling.

The film’s preview shows the artificial Kilmer as a thirty‑something figure whose performance appears rigid and lacks the actor’s voice and characteristic nuance. The release has sparked debate among experts, with some viewing the technology as a potential step toward reducing the need for flesh‑and‑blood performers, while others believe mainstream adoption remains uncertain.

In related news, the AI‑generated starlet Tilly Norwood is slated for her feature‑film debut, adding another example of digital characters entering the cinematic landscape. The differing opinions highlight ongoing discussion about how quickly AI might become a regular tool in mainstream filmmaking.
summary: An AI-created version of the late actor Val Kilmer, approved by his family, stars in the trailer for the western As Deep as the Grave directed by Coerte Voorhees. Experts are split on whether such technology could soon rival human film stars, and Kilmer’s estate said he was enthusiastic about new storytelling technology.
author: Guardian Technology

title: MI5 chief Sir Ken McCallum says AI could change bioweapon stakes
content: In his annual speech on threats to the nation, Sir Ken McCallum, the head of the UK’s intelligence service, MI5, warned that AI had the potential to ‘change the stakes’ on existing and even new bioweapons. To find out why, and how, Ian Sample speaks to Dr Tom Inglesby, director of the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security and the Bloomberg School of Public Health. He explains what has governments so worried and what measures could be put in place to reduce the risks Could AI ‘change the stakes’ in the development of bioweapons? Support the Guardian: theguardian. Com/sciencepod
summary: MI5 chief Sir Ken McCallum says AI could change bioweapon stakes.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Nasdaq 100 falls 5.5% as AI market faces reassessment
content:
After a wobble on the tech‑heavy Nasdaq, some AI market observers think a reassessment of the potential value of various businesses may be under way. The world is holding its breath as it waits to find out whether this year’s estimated $US1tn investment in artificial intelligence is resting on a castle made of sand.

Last week, the Nasdaq 100 – an index of the 100 biggest non‑financial stocks on the American tech‑heavy Nasdaq exchange – dropped by 5.5%, triggering the usual angst that the AI boom is about to go bust.
summary: The Nasdaq 100 index dropped 5.5% last week, prompting concerns about the AI boom. Some AI market observers say the decline may signal a reassessment of AI business values amid an estimated $US1tn AI investment this year.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI touted to save time is flooding inboxes with low‑quality content, says Gaby Hinsliff
content:
The Guardian columnist Gaby Hinsliff argues that the government’s promise of AI transforming the state has instead produced a “stream of machine‑generated slop.” She notes that, despite the claim that AI will streamline public services, the reality is that it has flooded inboxes with unwanted emails.

Hinsliff describes her own experience: after a “guilty cull,” her inbox still holds well over 7,000 messages. She likens the accumulation to the Quentin Crisp theory of housework, suggesting that empty inboxes quickly refill. The author points out that email was intended to save hours of meetings, phone calls, and photocopying, but now requires hours of deleting spam that would have otherwise been handled by a phone call.

She concludes that the convenience of reaching the world in seconds comes with the inconvenience of being able to be reached back with a single click, highlighting the unintended costs of the technology she once championed.
summary: The article notes the government claims AI can transform the state, yet the resulting wave of machine‑generated content is overwhelming. Guardian columnist Gaby Hinsliff observes her inbox holds over 7,000 messages, with AI‑driven spam undermining email’s intended time‑saving benefits.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Googlebook laptops launch at £999 but suffer software flaws, review says
content:
Google has introduced a new line of laptops called the Googlebook, designed to blend ChromeOS with Android features. The company aims to position these devices as competitors to Windows and macOS machines, offering advanced integration with Android phones and core Google services. In a review, the author notes that while the hardware is strong, software flaws detract from the overall experience.

The author tested two Googlebooks, noting that the devices are built by established PC manufacturers such as Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo. The price point for the entry‑level model starts at £999, equivalent to €1,099, $899, or A$2,299, which is significantly higher than the £160 price range typically associated with Chromebooks.

Compared to the budget‑friendly Chromebooks that have dominated the low‑cost laptop market for years, the Googlebook takes a premium approach. The review questions whether the new laptops can truly rival the performance and value offered by devices like the MacBook Air or the Surface Laptop.
summary: Google’s new laptops, called Googlebooks, combine ChromeOS with Android, are made by Acer, Asus, Dell, HP and Lenovo, and start at £999 (€1,099/$899/A$2,299). A review found the devices have strong hardware but are let down by software flaws, making them underbaked compared with competitors.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Google Cloud outage in London disrupts Revolut, bank customers report problems
content:
Google Cloud’s major outage in its London region has caused a ripple effect across the financial sector, with Revolut reporting a service disruption that has left many bank customers experiencing problems. The outage has highlighted the vulnerability of fintech platforms that rely on cloud infrastructure for day‑to‑day operations.

In other economic news, Britain’s unemployment rate fell unexpectedly to 4.7% this morning, prompting a rally in the pound. Sterling gained half a cent against the US dollar, trading at $1.3352, as the City welcomed the data that employment rose in the last quarter. The market reacted quickly, with traders scrambling to adjust exposure to the currency.

The labour market remains relatively flat overall, with resilience noted amid global headwinds. However, underlying challenges persist: about one million young people are not in education, employment or training, and overall employment is more than two million short of the Government’s 80 % target. The government has suggested that reforms to the benefit system are needed to provide active help and to make it easier for employers to create jobs.
summary: Google Cloud experienced a major outage in its London region. Revolut customers reported service disruptions as a result.
author: Guardian Technology

title: 14 dead, 7 injured in landslide at illegal gold mine in Narino, Colombia
content:
A landslide at an illegal gold mine in Colombia left at least 14 people dead and seven injured. The incident occurred in Narino, an area known as an illegal mining hotspot on the border with Ecuador.  

Armed groups in Narino control the clandestine gold trade there and are also involved in drug trafficking and extortion.
summary: At least 14 people were killed and seven injured when a landslide struck an illegal gold mine in Narino, Colombia. Armed groups in Narino, an illegal mining hotspot on the border with Ecuador, control the clandestine gold trade and are involved in drug trafficking and extortion.
author: Euronews

title: Paris police impose overnight curfew around Place de la Republique and Les Halles
content: Paris police imposed an overnight curfew on Monday around Place de la République and Les Halles following what officials described as France’s worst rioting in years. Officers patrolled the areas throughout the night, and the streets remained calm.
summary: Paris police imposed an overnight curfew on Monday around Place de la Republique and Les Halles after France’s worst rioting in years. Streets were calm.
author: Euronews

title: Ukraine's 92nd Assault Brigade conducts first drone evacuation of wounded soldier
content: Ukraine’s 92nd Assault Brigade has carried out its first aerial drone evacuation of a wounded soldier, pulling him from a position where mines and Russian drone activity made a conventional rescue impossible.
summary: The 92nd Assault Brigade of Ukraine says it performed its first aerial drone evacuation of a wounded soldier. The soldier was retrieved from a location where mines and Russian drone activity made a conventional rescue impossible.
author: Euronews

title: Japan launches MMX probe on H3 rocket to collect Phobos samples
content: Japan launched its MMX probe on Tuesday aboard the H3 rocket, beginning a three‑year mission to collect samples from Mars’s moon Phobos. The mission will return the material to Earth for analysis aimed at understanding the origins of the Solar System.
summary: Japan’s H3 rocket launched the MMX probe on Tuesday. The three-year mission will collect samples from Mars’s moon Phobos and study the origins of the Solar System.
author: Euronews

title: Alberta rejects plan for binding independence referendum; separatists vow to keep fighting
content: Alberta has rejected a proposal to hold a binding referendum on seceding from Canada. Following the decision, separatist supporters said they will continue to fight for independence.
summary: Alberta rejected a plan to hold a binding referendum on leaving Canada. Separatists vowed to keep fighting for independence.

content:
The midday bulletin for October 20, 2026 presents the most important stories from Europe and beyond. It covers the latest and breaking news across several domains.

title: Uzbekistan's $12bn business drive advances during Rubio visit
content:
Uzbekistan is advancing a $12 billion business initiative that spans railways, critical minerals, finance and technology, with major U.S. firms taking part, and the effort is gathering pace during a visit by Senator Rubio.  

President Shavkat Mirziyoyev outlined measures to attract investors, and business executives told Euronews that commercial activity is growing.
summary: The package covers railways, critical minerals, finance and technology, with major US firms involved. Uzbek President Mirziyoyev outlined measures to attract investors, while business executives told Euronews that commercial activity is growing.

content: Voters have decisively rejected a proposal to begin the legal process toward Alberta’s independence, delivering a major blow to a movement driven largely by economic grievances.

title: US investors boost acquisitions of Germany's traditional industrial and family firms
content: US investors are directing increasing capital toward Germany’s traditional industrial firms and family‑owned businesses. A shortage of successors among many owners is turning these companies into acquisition targets, prompting the rise in U.S. investment in the country’s famed Mittelstand.
summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family‑owned businesses. Many business owners are struggling to find successors, so more companies are becoming acquisition targets.
author: DW World

title: Subject to Change: A Dance for David Bowie to open at Sadler’s Wells in 2028
content: Subject to Change: A Dance for David Bowie will explore how the musician ‘practised a form of artistic reincarnation’, says choreographer Marcos Morau ‘Let’s dance,” sang David Bowie in 1983, commanding: “Put on your red shoes and dance the blues.” That call is to be answered – with footwear TBC – by an international dance production featuring new choral arrangements of songs from throughout his career. Subject to Change: A Dance for David Bowie will be staged at Sadler’s Wells in London in autumn 2028 after a world premiere in Luxembourg. It will visit Tokyo in 2029. The show will explore how Bowie “practised a form of artistic reincarnation” according to Spanish choreographer Marcos Morau who is taking inspiration from the superstar’s transformations into personas such as Aladdin Sane and the Thin White Duke.
summary: Subject to Change: A Dance for David Bowie to open at Sadler’s Wells in 2028.
author: Guardian World

title: Serbian prosecutor investigating Belgrade Trump tower targeted with spyware
content:
Serbian prosecutor Rade Bajić has investigated the authorities’ allegedly illegal scheme to help the Trumps build a tower in Belgrade.  

Expert analysis indicates an apparent attempt to hack Bajić’s iPhone with advanced spyware.  

The finding suggests a new element in the authoritarian Serbian regime’s campaign to undermine the criminal case, which critics describe as a “pay to play” scheme trading the Trump administration’s favour for business opportunities.
summary: A Serbian prosecutor, Rade Bajić, who investigated the Belgrade Trump tower project was targeted with advanced spyware. Expert analysis says the attempted hack of his iPhone reflects a new element in the Serbian regime’s campaign to undermine the criminal case linked to the Trump family’s alleged “pay to play” scheme.
author: Guardian World

title: French cities calm overnight after targeted curfews, prime minister says
content: The prime minister said French cities were “calm overnight” after targeted curfews were imposed. Sébastien Lecornu said more curfews could be introduced to quell unrest following weekend protests. According to BFMTV, the French parliament will consider formally opening an inquiry into the recent protests and violence, including the law‑enforcement measures used, after a political agreement was reached on the issue. Lecornu added that further information is expected in due course.
summary: The prime minister said French cities were calm overnight following targeted curfews. Sébastien Lecornu said more curfews may be introduced and parliament will consider opening an inquiry into the recent protests and violence, BFMTV reported.
author: Guardian World

title: Italy to deploy 500 troops to Milan after protests turn violent
content:
Italy’s government announced it will send 500 soldiers to Milan following several days of protests over the high cost of living that turned violent, with clashes against police, vandalism and looting. The deployment is intended as a “firm response from the state” ahead of additional demonstrations scheduled for Saturday.

According to reports in the Italian press on Tuesday, the administration led by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni plans to fast‑track new security measures, including extending preventive detention for minors, targeting youth gangs and banning gatherings deemed a threat to public order.
summary: Italy's government is sending 500 soldiers to Milan after protests against the high cost of living descended into clashes, vandalism and looting. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government plans to swiftly approve tougher security measures, including extending preventive detention for minors, cracking down on youth gangs and banning gatherings deemed a threat to public order.
author: Guardian World

title: Victorian coroner says online betting caused 22-year-old Kyle Hudson's suicide
content: Online betting was the ‘direct and paramount’ cause behind Kyle Hudson’s decision to take his own life, inquest finds Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Kyle Hudson was “a young man brimming with promise”, with a loving and supportive partner, family and friends, and prospects. “It was a near ideal picture – except for the grip that online sports betting had upon him,” the Victorian coroner Paul Lawrie said on Tuesday.
summary: The Victorian coroner Paul Lawrie found that online sports betting was the direct and paramount cause of Kyle Hudson’s suicide. Hudson, a 22‑year‑old described as a young man with a supportive partner, family and prospects, was said to have been dominated by gambling.

title: Brendan Nugent charged with three offences after alleged attack on MP Helen Haines
content:
Victoria police arrested 43‑year‑old Brendan Nugent of Tarrawingee on Monday afternoon following an incident in Wangaratta involving Member of Parliament Helen Haines. Nugent has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the Commonwealth offence of causing harm to a Commonwealth public official. He will be held overnight and is scheduled to appear at Wangaratta Magistrates Court on Wednesday, with police stating the alleged attack was targeted.

Nugent’s family said Haines has been a friend of theirs for more than 20 years.
summary: Brendan Nugent charged with three offences after alleged attack on MP Helen Haines.
author: Guardian World

title: Helen Haines, independent MP attacked, has been friend of Brendan Nugent’s family for 20+ years
content:
Brendan Nugent’s family said they have known independent MP Helen Haines for more than 20 years. The father of a 43‑year‑old man from Tarrawingee, who has been charged with allegedly attacking Haines, pledged to cooperate with police and described the incident as “shocking and horrific”. He called the event “devastating and unfathomable”.

Haines was airlifted from Wangaratta in northern Victoria to Melbourne’s Alfred Hospital for emergency surgery on Monday night. On Tuesday she remained in critical condition, having lost one leg while surgeons worked to save the other.
summary: Helen Haines was airlifted to Melbourne after being attacked, lost one leg and remains in critical condition while surgeons work to save the other. Brendan Nugent’s family say they have been friends with Haines for more than 20 years.
author: Guardian World

title: Alberta voters reject independence referendum, 76% choose to stay in Canada
content: Alberta voters have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to start a process toward independence, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta. More than 1.5 million votes have been counted, with 76 % supporting remaining in Canada and roughly 24 % backing a move toward separation. The outcome was described as a victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity.
summary: Alberta voters overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to start a process toward independence, a result hailed as a victory for prime minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity. Unofficial results from Elections Alberta show about 76% voted to remain in Canada and roughly 24% backed separation.

title: Study finds moon's radius shrank about 148 feet based on 10,000 surface cracks
content:
Scientists have determined that the Moon is slowly shrinking, a conclusion reached through a detailed analysis of images taken by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC). In the new study, researchers identified more than 10,000 young faults—cracks that have formed in the last several hundred million years—across the lunar surface. By cataloguing these features, the team was able to calculate how much the Moon’s radius has decreased over time.

The study estimates that the Moon’s radius has contracted by about 148 feet (45 meters) over the past 400 to 800 million years. Lead author Thomas Watters, a geologist and scientist emeritus at the Center for Earth and Planetary Studies at the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum, noted that the number of young faults revealed in the LROC images far exceeds his expectations. He added that as the Moon’s interior continues to cool and contract, the growth of existing faults and the formation of new ones is likely to continue.

The faults mapped in the study include lobate scarps—long, curved structures that form when the Moon’s surface contracts, cracks, and is pushed upward—and small mare ridges, narrow “wrinkles” found on the dark plains. Unlike Earth, which has about 15 major tectonic plates, the Moon is a single‑plate body; its outer shell is a single piece broken only by faults created by contraction.

By mapping thousands of these features, the researchers pieced together aspects of lunar history. They found that some regions of the Moon contain many more faults than others, and that areas with fewer cracks have thicker crust. This suggests that the thicker crust in those regions has been more stable, and that many of the widespread cracks were created later in the Moon’s history, after its early, thicker crust had insulated the interior and slowed cooling.

The findings were published on Oct. 14 in The Planetary Science Journal.
summary: Scientists analyzing Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera images identified over 10,000 young faults on the Moon’s surface. From these features they estimate the Moon’s radius has decreased by about 148 feet (45 meters) over the past 400 to 800 million years.
author: Space.com

title: Europe's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli lander arrive at Mars on Oct. 19, 2016
content:
On October 19, 2016, the European Space Agency’s ExoMars 2016 mission arrived at Mars, comprising the Trace Gas Orbiter and the Schiaparelli lander. Launched in March 2016, the spacecraft traveled together before separating on October 16, three days prior to the orbiter entering orbit. The mission was designed to test landing techniques for a future rover and deliver an orbiter to study the Martian atmosphere. Ultimately, the mission was described by ESA officials as "96% successful" due to the loss of the lander.

While the Trace Gas Orbiter successfully entered orbit, the Schiaparelli lander crashed during its descent. It stopped communicating with Earth one minute before its planned landing. Photos from NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter later revealed what appeared to be the crash site and a jettisoned parachute nearby. Officials suspect that a data glitch prevented Schiaparelli from firing its descent thrusters, which were necessary to slow the craft for a safe landing.

The Trace Gas Orbiter remains functional and continues to circle Mars, searching for methane and other gases that could indicate biological activity. The failure of Schiaparelli, combined with the loss of the Russian Proton rocket after ESA severed its partnership with Russia over the war in Ukraine, delayed the ExoMars 2018 mission. This mission includes the Mars rover Rosalind Franklin and is now expected to launch no earlier than 2028, with a landing on Mars anticipated in 2030.

The article also notes that on October 19, 2026, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency attempted to launch the Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX. This mission aims to land a probe on the Mars moon Phobos and return samples to Earth.
summary: On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars mission arrived at Mars!
author: Space.com

title: Lego X‑Files Set Brings 90s Sci‑Fi Nostalgia to Fans
content: Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. It's easy to see why we yearn for the days of Pogs, the Backstreet Boys, and Saved by the Bell. One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi, when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services. You can relive those glory days of alien conspiracies, spooky happenings and cell phones the size of a brick with the Lego Ideas The X-Files set. This 1478 piece set is essentially two dioramas crammed into a single display piece. The top of the model depicts a spinning UFO floating above one of those iconic coniferous forests that dominated 90s sci-fi. Why? Because — thanks to some generous tax credits — it was cheaper to shoot in Vancouver, so that's where they all flocked. Disney Plus / Hulu bundle: was $12.99 now $11.99 Catch Mulder and Scully in every season of The X-Files on Hulu, which is available bundled with Disney+ for only $11.99/month for the first six months, then increasing to $12.99/month. View Deal Mulder and Scully closing in on our "Grey" alien friend in the woods. (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) Beneath the woodland scene, though, is the real star of the show: Mulder's office, squirrelled away in the basement of the FBI's J. Edgar Hoover Building in Washington, D. C. This dingy little office is where Scully meets "Spooky Mulder", kicking off a glorious sci-fi odyssey that would last for eleven seasons (and two movies). Mulder's dingy little base of operations has been stunningly recreated here, with both overt references and subtle nods that X-Files fans will appreciate. The iconic "I want to believe" poster adorns the wall, alongside photographs of crop circles and a newspaper clipping from a paper called "The Lone Brickman" — a nice nod to " The Lone Gunmen ". There's even an actual X-File sitting on the desk, and a cute Lego spoof of the "Face on Mars", with a photo on the wall that shows a Lego head on the moon. The X-Files Complete Boxset: $160 Prefer to actually own your media? Make your way through this X-Files Complete Boxset on DVD. Just bear in mind that you will need a region-free DVD player to watch it with. The iconic "I Want To Believe" poster. Future (Ian Stokes) Newspaper clippings were a staple of the X-Files office. Future (Ian Stokes) The show's legendary tagline is proudly displayed on the front. Future (Ian Stokes) X(Files) marks the spot. Future (Ian Stokes) It's been a hot minute since I watched The X-Files (that DVD box set beside my TV is calling to me), but even so, I had a blast building my way down memory lane, remembering episodes as I assembled the diorama. I love the little touches, like the display cabinets filled with artifacts, the VHS tapes scattered around the office and the black oil spillage on the floor. As with most Lego sets, the minifigures are half the joy. You get Mulder and Scully, obviously, with the dynamic duo of FBI agents both rocking flashlights (no smartphones with built-in lights back in the 90s). Mulder is wearing dark blue, while Scully is rocking an orangey brown suit, with both of them sporting an FBI badge. Outside of the principal pair, you also get Skinner, Mr X, and the Cigarette Smoking Man. Mulder's partner-turned-nemesis Alex Krycek also gets a suitably devious-looking minifig. It's the gloves, they just make him look like a bad man (which, to be fair, he is). Finally, to ramp up the paranormal scale, we also get a pair of monster minifigs: a grey alien and Flukeman minifigures. The grey alien was a must-have, especially given the UFO floating atop this display piece, but the one-off monster of the week, Flukeman, felt like a weird choice. Agents Mulder and Scully, FBI. Future (Ian Stokes) Assistant Director Skinner, Mr X, and the Cigarette Smoking Man in Mulder's Office. Future (Ian Stokes) Also, this John Doggett erasure will not stand. Sure, he could never replace Mulder, but Robert Patrick's seasons eight and nine run was excellent and he deserved a spot here. And while I'm voicing minor gripes, the usual Lego FOMO tricks were in force with this set; if you pre-ordered, you got an exclusive gift set — Scully's Lab — free of charge. This extra little diorama isn't necessary, but it does feel like the collection is incomplete without it and it's not for sale separately, so you'll have to try your luck with eBay scalpers if you want it. Speaking of Scully, Gillian Anderson has stated that after season 11 wrapped in 2018, she was done with the role. That wasn't entirely accurate, though, as she donned the lab gloves one more time for the Lego X-Files set advert. It's a short bit of fan service, but a nice touch, and, once again, it sparks those 90s neurons. All these delicious Member Berries come at a price, though, and that's the price. This blast from the past will set you back $199 (£179 in the UK). That's no small chunk of change. But then again, anyone who wants this set is in their thirties or forties and can probably afford that outlay for the nostalgia trip. And look at it this way: when The X-Files debuted back in 1993, the price would only have been about $86. I had a great time building the Lego X-Files set and if you're a fan of the series, you will too. Nostalgia often feels like a cheat code to our hearts, but there's nothing wrong with that. We deserve to remember the good times and the truth is that The X-Files was about as good as it ever got for sci-fi fans. You can buy the Lego X-Files set now, available for $199/£179 from the Lego store.
summary: The 1478‑piece Lego X‑Files set recreates a UFO‑hovering forest and Mulder’s basement office and includes minifigures of Mulder, Scully, Skinner, Mr X, the Cigarette Smoking Man, Alex Krycek, a grey alien and Flukeman. Pre‑orders receive a free Scully’s Lab diorama, and the set is priced at $199 and sold through the Lego store.

title: A Zack Snyder DC Universe might not have been such a bad thing, after all
content: After Joss Whedon’s arrival, back in the news with comments from Ben Affleck, the franchise lost a sense of earnest passion that could have sustained a weary DCEU Nine years after superhero epic Justice League arrived in cinemas, there ought to be very little left to say about how it all went wrong. Zack Snyder shot the film, Joss Whedon substantially rewrote and reshot it, and audiences eventually got to see both men’s versions. Any debate over their relative merits long ago disappeared. Whedon is pretty much cancelled; Snyder has reinvented himself as the writer-director of extremely average ersatz Star Wars movies for Netflix, and an entirely new DC universe is under way that has very little to do with either of them. To a greater or lesser extent, the world has moved on. But Ben Affleck’s latest comments raise an uncomfortable question about whether Snyder’s departure was ever presented honestly. Speaking to Josh Horowitz on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, Affleck, who played Batman, described the Justice League reshoots as the lowest point of his career, but reserved his strongest criticism for the circumstances of Snyder’s departure. The director stepped away in May 2017, two months after his daughter Autumn killed herself, aged 20, with the public explanation that he needed to be with his family. Affleck, however, alleged that studio Warner Bros had used the tragedy to justify replacing him. “The way in which that was, I thought, used as an excuse was one of the shittiest things I’ve ever seen,” Affleck said. “It was so gross.”
summary: A Zack Snyder DC Universe might not have been such a bad thing, after all.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Ed Sanders: 87‑year‑old counterculture icon who tried to topple the Pentagon
content: He gave Jimi Hendrix his gear, freaked out Frank Sinatra, inspired Norman Mailer – and tried to topple the American war machine. As a documentary about his band the Fugs comes out, the 87-year-old gives a rare interview “Charles Manson once wrote me a letter saying, ‘If I was as powerful as you claim then you wouldn’t be here,’” Ed Sanders tells me over a video call, savouring the menace in that sentence. Sanders is an American maverick; a musician, poet, activist, journalist and author whose greatest hit remains his bestselling 1971 book The Family, in which he chronicled the lives, crimes and trials of Manson and his followers. Sanders was well placed to report on crazed hippies, having played a pivotal role in launching the US counterculture – though he very much espoused peace, love and consciousness-raising, rather than Manson’s apocalyptic worldview.
summary: Ed Sanders: 87‑year‑old counterculture icon who tried to topple the Pentagon.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Review: Life Out of Order fails to recapture Niffenegger's original spark
content: More than two decades on, the passion that ignited Niffenegger’s debut has all but evaporated from this confused follow-up I run a reading workshop which begins with a little shelf assessment. Participants bring a stack of books that have shaped who they are: childhood treasures; new revelations; comfort reads. Books they once cherished but have now outgrown. The usual suspect in that category is Audrey Niffenegger’s 2003 novel The Time Traveler’s Wife. Once smitten, readers now find that time-warped romance cruel. What felt like destiny now feels like a cage. As they explain, I’m always struck by the same thought: Wasn’t it always cruel? Wasn’t that the point? Henry DeTamble and Clare Abshire are a couple caught in a causal loop. The irresolvable question is where that loop starts: does a bright young art student fall in love with a junior librarian, or does a time-travelling man groom a child to become his future wife? If the answer is both – and it has to be – what are we to make of their marriage? Can you truly choose someone if you believe the choice is already made?
summary: The reviewer notes that the passion that ignited Niffenegger’s debut has all but evaporated from this confused follow‑up. They describe how readers who once cherished The Time Traveler’s Wife now find its time‑warped romance cruel.
author: Guardian Culture

title: With nine new recordings of Mahler’s epic Resurrection Symphony this year alone, which rises above the rest?
content: The second – the ‘Resurrection’ – was the first Mahler symphony ever to be recorded, and it is still today an essential work in any conductor’s catalogue. But with hundreds of recordings, from Ormandy to Bernstein and Rattle, which does our reviewer recommend? Is it something in the water? Or is it simply that triumph over adversity sells in today’s uncertain world? Whatever the reason, Mahler’s Resurrection Symphony has already received four major UK performances this year: a season finale for the BBC Philharmonic in Manchester, a season opener for both the City of Birmingham Symphony Orchestra and the London Symphony Orchestra, and an 80th season celebratory concert for the Philharmonia Orchestra in London. Next month the London City Orchestra perform it in Croydon’s Fairfield Halls. On disc, the field of Mahler 2s is even more crowded. Apple Music Classical currently throws up 222 listings; Presto Music ’s search engine returns 260 results, many of them complete recordings to download or buy on CD or vinyl (some of these, of course, are reissues of recognised classic accounts).
summary: The second – the ‘Resurrection’ – was the first Mahler symphony ever to be recorded, and it is still today an essential work in any conductor’s catalogue. But with hundreds of recordings, from Ormandy to Bernstein and Rattle, which does our reviewer recommend?
author: Guardian Culture

title: Linda Cardellini Talks Horror Role as Pamela Voorhees in Friday the 13th Prequel
content: She got to torment Don Draper in Mad Men and has just won an Emmy for DTF St Louis. But nothing prepared the star for all the gore as she switched to horror with the Friday the 13th prequel ‘The first time I had the tooth in my hand,” says Linda Cardellini, “I thought, ‘Oh my God, this is what I’m doing.’” The star of Freaks and Geeks, ER, Dead to Me, Mad Men and DTF St Louis (for which she recently won an Emmy) is talking about her pivot towards full-blown horror. In Crystal Lake, the prequel to the Friday the 13th movies, Cardellini plays Pamela Voorhees, the original slasher of the 1980 film. The tooth, by the way, is human and gets embedded in Pam’s knuckle – until she yanks it out with a gruesome, revolting slurping sound. Casual filmgoers may associate Friday the 13th with Jason, the hockey-mask-wearing serial killer. But aficionados will know that Pam, Jason’s mother, is the villain of the first movie. “He didn’t even have the mask until the third movie,” says Cardellini, who has clearly done her homework. “Pam is the original killer, in vengeance of his death.” (There is some massaging of previous storylines in Crystal Lake, such as moving Jason’s drowning from the 1950s to the early 70s, but since the franchise is flexible enough to have sent Jason into space at one point, a bit of timeline tweaking feels fair game.)
summary: Linda Cardellini discussed her new horror role as Pamela Voorhees in the Friday the 13th prequel 'Crystal Lake' and described the gore she experienced. She also highlighted her recent Emmy win for DTF St Louis and her past work on Freaks and Geeks, ER, Dead to Me, and Mad Men.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Nathan Fielder's 'You Can See Everything' on Elizabeth Holmes becomes sold‑out hit
content:
Nathan Fielder’s new A24 documentary, You Can See Everything, has emerged as a sold-out hit, with reports suggesting it may make Oscars history. The film, which was previously shrouded in secrecy, centers on the Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes. A pivotal moment in the three-hour movie involves Fielder asking Holmes, “Are you being real right now?” during a close-up shot that highlights their intense eye contact. This question underscores the narrative, particularly in the film’s first half, which gained attention following the project’s announcement in September.

The initial segment of the documentary takes place entirely in 2023, depicting Fielder and co-director Lance Oppenheim, along with a small crew, embedding with Holmes, her husband Billy Evans, and their two young children. This period occurred in the run-up to Holmes’s prison sentence for fraud. Over several weeks in a beachfront rental, Fielder attempts to challenge Holmes’s facade of faultlessness. The dynamic is described as a surreal chess game between Fielder, an absurdist auteur known for his deadpan style, and Holmes, a skilled fabricator, with Evans present alongside them.

While not strictly comedic, the interaction is noted for its humor and tension, resembling the disorienting pull of an internet wormhole. The film explores the lack of outside context that surrounds Holmes, raising questions about the sincerity of her statements. For instance, Holmes told Fielder with apparent sincerity that she has never told a lie in her life. She also maintained, despite contrary reality, that Theranos devices were capable of performing 1,000 diagnostic tests. These moments illustrate the claustrophobic nature of the first half of the film, which remains the primary focus for viewers adhering to spoiler guidelines.
summary: The A24 documentary 'You Can See Everything' directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim has sold out and might make Oscars history. The film follows Fielder and a small crew embedding with Elizabeth Holmes, her husband Billy Evans, and their two children in 2023 as they prepare for her prison sentence for fraud.

content:

Monfils, a French star, has also recently retired after a glittering career.

content: 28-year-old set to miss season after diagnosis Tanner McKee has taken over as Eagles starter Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is set to miss the rest of the season after further testing ⁠revealed blood clots had traveled from his leg to his lungs, the team announced on Monday. title: Scott Boland takes four wickets as rain delays South Africa's second Test
content:
Scott Boland delivered a strong performance in the second Test at Gqeberha, taking four wickets by the end of the day. The match was heavily affected by rain, with play delayed until deep into the afternoon on both days. When the wet outfield finally dried, South Africa were reduced to 97‑5.

Boland’s wickets came in quick succession. He finished an over he had started the day before at 3:45 pm, six hours after the scheduled start. Four balls were bowled, one of which was a boundary from Temba Bavuma. Boland’s aggressive line invites such shots while he searches for an edge.

Earlier in the match, Boland had dismissed Aiden Markram and David Bedingham. Seven balls into day two, he added Marques Ackerman to the tally.
summary: Veteran fast bowler Scott Boland claimed four wickets as South Africa were dismissed for 97-5 on day two of the second Test at Gqeberha. Rain delayed play until the afternoon, with the outfield drying enough for the match to resume.
